seoTitle: Fence Calculator - Estimate Wood & Chain Link Materials
metaDescription: Free online Fence Calculator. Easily determine how many posts, pickets, rails, and panels you need to enclose your yard with a new privacy fence.
secondaryKeywords: how many fence panels do I need
intro: Securing your backyard for a new dog? Our free Fence Calculator removes the complex math from fence building, telling you exactly how many posts, panels, or individual pickets you need to buy.
whatIs: The Fence Calculator is an outdoor construction estimation utility. It takes the linear perimeter of your property and divides it by standard fencing measurements to generate a comprehensive bill of materials.
howToUse: Enter the total linear footage of the fence line to be built.
Select your fence type (Pre-built Panels or 'Stick-built' individual pickets).
Enter your post spacing (typically 6 or 8 feet).
The tool calculates the required posts, concrete bags, rails, and pickets.
howItWorks: The tool divides the total linear length by the post spacing to determine the number of posts (adding 1 for the end post). If stick-building, it multiplies the number of sections by the rails per section (usually 3). It then divides the total length by the width of a single picket to find the picket count.
workedExample: You need 100 feet of privacy fence using standard 8-foot pre-built panels. 100 / 8 = 12.5. You will need 13 panels. You will also need 14 posts to hold those 13 panels up, and 14 bags of concrete.
resultInterpretation: The output is a precise shopping list. It prevents the common DIY mistake of forgetting the final end post or underestimating the number of 2x4 rails needed to support the pickets.
useCases: Home Enclosures: A homeowner estimating the cost difference between an 8-foot spaced panel fence vs a custom 6-foot spaced picket fence.
Property Lines: Calculating the materials required to replace a single 40-foot span of fence blown down in a storm.
Budgeting: Taking the exact picket count and multiplying it by the cost of cedar vs pine to determine project affordability.
tipsAndLimitations: Always add an extra post for every gate you plan to install, as gates require dedicated hinge and latch posts.
If your property is on a steep hill, 'stepped' fencing requires more posts and shorter panel spans than flat ground.

faq.question: How deep should fence posts go?
faq.answer: A general rule is that 1/3 of the total post length should be buried in the ground. For a 6-foot tall fence, you need an 8-foot post, burying 2 feet of it in concrete.

faq.question: Should I use panels or individual pickets?
faq.answer: Panels are much faster to install but require perfectly flat ground. Stick-building with individual pickets takes longer but allows the fence to perfectly follow the natural slope of your yard.

disclaimer: Tool estimates assume flat terrain and straight property lines. Local building codes may require specific post depths or wind-load reinforcements not accounted for here.
